[[United States]] | website = {{URL|https://creation.com/}} }} '''Creation Ministries International''' ('''CMI''') is a [[nonprofit organisation]] that promotes the [[pseudoscience]] of [[young Earth creationism]].{{cite web|url=http://creation.com/should-genesis-be-taken-literally|title=Should Genesis be taken literally |publisher=creation.com|accessdate=4 February 2016}}{{third-party-inline|date=February 2016}} It has branches in [[Australia]], [[Canada]], [[New Zealand]], [[Singapore]], [[South Africa]], the [[United Kingdom]], and the [[United States]].{{cite web|url=http://creation.com/contactus|title=Worldwide Contact Information |publisher=creation.com|accessdate=4 February 2016}}{{third-party-inline|date=February 2016}}{{cite journal|last1=Ruse|first1=Michael|title=Creation Science is not Science|journal= Science, Technology, & Human Values|date=15 July 1982|volume=7|issue=3|pages=10–18|doi=10.1177/016224398200700313|s2cid=143503427}} == History == In 1977, [[Carl Wieland]] organised the Creation Science Association (CSA) in [[Adelaide]] in [[South Australia]]. In 1978, the organisation began the magazine ''Ex Nihilo'' (from the [[Latin (language)|Latin]] phrase ''[[creatio ex nihilo]]'', meaning "creation out of nothing"). Soon after, the Creation Science Foundation (CSF) took over production of ''Ex Nihilo'' (later renaming it ''Creation Ex Nihilo'', and eventually simply ''Creation''). In 1984, CSF started the ''Ex Nihilo Technical Journal'' for more in-depth analysis of creationist issues (it was later renamed ''Creation Ex Nihilo Technical Journal'', then simply ''TJ'', and now the ''Journal of Creation''). In the mid-1990s, [[Ken Ham]], formerly of the Creation Science Foundation and then part of the [[Institute for Creation Research]], formed an autonomous ministry in the United States. This ministry, along with the Australian Creation Science Foundation, was branded "[[Answers in Genesis]]" (AiG); eventually, legally autonomous Answers in Genesis offices were opened in Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, and the United Kingdom. Following a legal dispute in 2005,{{cite web |url=http://ncse.com/news/2007/06/answers-genesis-legal-turmoil-001080 |title=Answers in Genesis in legal turmoil |author= |date=June 21, 2007 |publisher=[[National Center for Science Education]] |location=Berkeley, CA |access-date=April 6, 2008}} AiG split in 2006. The Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and South Africa branches re-branded as "Creation Ministries International".[https://creation.com/about-us#history Creation Ministries International – About us, history] In late 2006, CMI established offices in the UK and the United States. Since then, CMI has distributed ''Creation'' magazine and the ''Journal of Creation'' in the United States itself. CMI publishes ''Creation'' magazine and the ''Journal of Creation''. ''Creation'' reports that it has subscribers in more than 170 countries,{{cite web|url= http://creation.com/creation-magazine|title= Creation magazine |publisher= creation.com |accessdate= 4 February 2016}}{{third-party-inline |date= February 2016}}{{third-party-inline|date= February 2016}} with 60,000 copies of each issue produced. [http://www1.auspost.com.au/priority/index.asp?issue_id=13&area=features&article_id=285] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003144937/http://www1.auspost.com.au/priority/index.asp?issue_id=13&area=features&article_id=285|date=3 October 2009}} ''Creation'' is published four times a year. The ''Journal of Creation'' is published three times a year; CMI claims that it is peer reviewed, but the scientific community does not consider this to be so since the peer review is only held within a closed circle of CMI members and the peer reviewers for issues are not disclosed for verification of peer review rigor.{{cn|date=October 2026}} == ''The Voyage That Shook the World'' == {{Main|The Voyage That Shook the World}} ''The Voyage That Shook The World'' is a 2009 dramatised documentary film commissioned by Creation Ministries International and produced by Fathom Media. It was released to mark the 200th anniversary of [[Charles Darwin]]'s birth and the 150th anniversary of the publication of his seminal work ''[[On the Origin of Species]]''.{{cite web|url=http://www.ballymoneytimes.co.uk/churches/39The-Voyage-that-shook-the.5351195.jp|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121209133710/http://www.ballymoneytimes.co.uk/churches/39The-Voyage-that-shook-the.5351195.jp|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 December 2012|title=The Voyage that shook the world|publisher=ballymoneytimes.co.uk|accessdate=4 February 2016}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/ni/2009/06/creationists_defend_darwin_fil.html|title=BBC – Will & Testament: Creationists defend Darwin film|publisher=BBC|accessdate=4 February 2016}} This 52-minute-long film includes interviews with proponents of [[intelligent design]] and [[young Earth creationism]] along with some scholars, academics, and scientists who support the [[scientific consensus]] on [[evolution]]. Some of the mainstream scientists later said that the filmmakers deceptively edited their interviews and misled them. It features wildlife footage from the [[Galapagos Islands]] as well as on-location footage from Argentina, Chile, [[Tierra del Fuego]], and the United Kingdom. The film's dramatised sequences were shot on location in [[Tasmania]], Australia. The [[National Center for Science Education]] reviewed the film and found it misleading.{{cite news |title=Screen Australia film agency awarded creationist film AUD$90,000 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2015/apr/29/australian-film-agency-awarded-creationist-film-aud90000-anti-evolution |access-date=19 August 2021 |work=The Guardian |date=29 April 2015}} == Legal controversy with Answers in Genesis == CMI's history is closely linked with that of its daughter ministry in the United States, [[Answers in Genesis]] (AiG), founded by former Australian colleague [[Ken Ham]]. A legal and personal dispute broke out between the Australian and US arms of AiG in 2005, involving claims of unethical dealing in handling magazine subscriptions and autocratic leadership on Ham's part. A more involved analysis of the situation is described in an account in the ''Reports of the National Center for Science Education''.{{cite journal | author = Lippard, Jim | year = 2006 | title = Trouble in Paradise: Answers in Genesis Splinters | journal = Reports of the National Center for Science Education | volume = 26 | issue = 6, November | pages = 4–7 | url=https://ncse.com/library-resource/trouble-paradise | accessdate=4 February 2016| author-link = Jim Lippard }} A lawsuit was filed on 31 May 2007, by CMI in [[Supreme Court of Queensland]] against Ken Ham and Answers in Genesis, seeking damages and accusing "unbiblical/unethical/unlawful behaviour" in Ham's dealings with the Australian organisation.{{cite web |url=http://theaustralian.news.com.au/story/0%2C20867%2C21843706-2702%2C00.html?from=public_rss |title=Biblical battle of creation groups | the Nation |website=[[The Australian]] |access-date=15 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070610120854/http://theaustralian.news.com.au/story/0%2C20867%2C21843706-2702%2C00.html?from=public_rss |archive-date=10 June 2007 |url-status=dead}} CMI produces ''Creation Magazine'' and the ''Journal of Creation'', formerly distributed by the US and UK AiG offices to their respective countries prior to the split. The Australian group maintains it was disconnected from all its American subscribers when the US office "announced on its web site (without telling us, the publishers) that it was ceasing to distribute both of these publications (and simultaneously announced its own magazine)". CMI further alleged in the lawsuit that AiG misrepresented their own magazine to subscribers as a replacement for ''Creation''. CMI is claiming $252,000 (US) in damages for lost revenue by misleading and deceptive conduct in relating to lost subscriptions.[http://www.ecourts.courts.qld.gov.au/eSearching/filedetails.asp?FileNumber=4690%2F07&Court=Supreme&Location=BRISB] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706122047/http://www.ecourts.courts.qld.gov.au/eSearching/filedetails.asp?FileNumber=4690%2F07&Court=Supreme&Location=BRISB|date=6 July 2011}} The case also concerns use of the trademark "Answers in Genesis" within Australia, and alleged misuse by Ken Ham of his position as a director for the Australian group to cause it detriment. Answers in Genesis had little to say in public to these accusations, but in comments to news reporters, Ken Ham dismissed them all as "totally preposterous and untrue". In February 2009, the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit]] ordered Australian-based Creation Ministries International into arbitration in the United States with Answers in Genesis (as sought by AiG) over copyrights and control of affiliates in other countries.{{cite news | author = Lovan, Dylan T. | year = 2009 | title = Court: Creationists Should Settle Outside Court | newspaper = Taiwan News | format = online | issue = 14 February | agency = Associated Press | url = http://www.etaiwannews.com/etn/news_content.php?id=865750&lang=eng_newsOnline | accessdate = 4 February 2016 | archive-date = 5 February 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160205000013/http://www.etaiwannews.com/etn/news_content.php?id=865750&lang=eng_newsOnline | url-status = dead }}{{cite court |litigants=Answers in Genesis of Kentucky v. Creation Ministries International, Ltd. | vol= |reporter= |opinion=08-6014/6032 |pinpoint= | ref = File Name: 09a0055p.06 | court=6th Cir. |year=2009 |url=http://www.ca6.uscourts.gov/opinions.pdf/09a0055p-06.pdf | access-date = 4 February 2016 |quote=For the foregoing reasons, we affirm the judgment of the district court in its entirety. Our affirmance as to the district court's refusal to issue a foreign antisuit injunction is without prejudice so that AiG may renew its motion before the district court should proceedings in the Australian suit resume. We also deny CMI's motion to stay arbitration as moot in light of our disposition of this appeal. ([[United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit]]) }} In April 2009, the ministries reached a settlement and ended their dispute.{{cite web |url=https://ncse.ngo/creationist-legal-dispute-resolved |title=Creationist legal dispute resolved |author= |date=April 29, 2009 |publisher=National Center for Science Education |access-date=May 21, 2021 }} == Relationship with schools == In 2011, a group of 30 UK scientists accused the organisation's representatives of falsely presenting themselves to schools as scientists.{{cite news |last1=Butt |first1=Riazat |title=Scientists demand tougher guidelines on teaching of creationism in schools |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2011/sep/19/scientists-demand-guidelines-creationism-schools |access-date=19 August 2021 |work=The Guardian |date=19 September 2011}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * {{Official website|https://creation.com}} {{Creation Science}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:1977 establishments in Australia]] [[Category:Christian organizations established in 1977]] [[Category:Creation science]] [[Category:Creationist organizations]] [[Category:Young Earth creationism]]
